treatments.rationale: Explains the Stieltjes increment measure using an admissible piecewise-linear candidate, a constant positive candidate and a densely atomic example. These examples distinguish support, pointwise positivity and density; they are not asserted to be minimisers.

States the selected support theorem under the pure zero-field covariance convention and an admissible integrable minimiser. Existence of a minimiser and the additional density and circuit conclusions are outside this statement.
States full support relative to [0,1) and strict increase under the displayed minimiser hypotheses. The excluded endpoint one and the restriction to pure zero-field SK remain explicit.

States both saturated moment identities for every associated diffusion and every 0<=t<1 under the theorem hypotheses. The statement does not make those identities definitions for arbitrary admissible candidates.

States the admissible one-sided derivative formula and explains the separate penalty and reoptimised-control contributions. Nonnegativity of the derivative requires a minimiser; the cited formula itself applies to admissible coefficients and feasible directions.

Applies the derivative formula to gamma=0 and the feasible constant direction, obtaining a negative cost and hence a nonminimising example. The calculation does not apply a minimiser-only contact or saturation conclusion.

Uses the general moment identity with the explicit heat curvature to calculate q0 prime and q0. The displayed value q0(1/2)=1/3 distinguishes that general identity from the minimiser-only identity q=t.

Reports the additional smooth positive-density conclusion and directs its derivation to the source corollary and long record. This further-reading passage does not supply the smoothness or fixed-time replacement proof.

Directs the reader to the terminal-martingale value argument while distinguishing its first curvature moment from the second-moment identity used in the no-gap explanation. The scalar identity is not derived in this passage.

Identifies the separate circuit theorem, its earlier conjecture and the long-record destination. This reference-only passage does not replace the quantified theorem or its additional construction with full support alone.

reading_links.rationale: Answers the tilted-endpoint-chord exercise and contrasts strict with non-strict convexity. This is a standalone calculus example, not an SK moment curve or an instance of the graph lemma requiring both endpoint slopes to be at most one.

The elementary Gaussian correction illustrates changing the visible sign while preserving expectation through a vanishing boundary term. It supplies none of the SK-specific joint shape restrictions, rational certificate or coercive estimate.

Uses the zero coefficient and a feasible constant direction to make the one-sided variation test concrete. Its negative derivative demonstrates failure of minimality and does not instantiate a minimiser-only conclusion.
